To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the data-intensive workflow systems use different approaches for processing huge amounts of data, such as using distributed file systems and distributed data storage, using distributed data processing, and using data transfer and caching; (2) the data-intensive systems use different scheduling algorithms and heuristics for optimizing different objectives, such as makespan and cost; (3) the data-intensive workflows systems use different approaches and heuristics to minimize network usage, such as using data transfer, caching, and replication; and

(a) the performance and efficiency of data-intensive applications can be improved by using workflow management techniques, and (b) the efficiency can be further improved by using workflow scheduling techniques.
the following factors affect the performance of data intensive workflows: (i) data size and volume, (ii) data access pattern, and (iii) data transfer rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, development and implementation of algorithms and techniques for the efficient execution of data-intensive scientific application workflows in distributed environments.
the development of a novel framework for the scheduling and management of large-scale data-intensive workflows in the cloud.

the following issues: 1) how to schedule data-intensive workflows onto distributed resources to meet the application requirements; 2) how to manage data transfers to minimize the network bandwidth and cost of data transfers; 3) how to optimize the workflow schedule to meet the application deadline; 4) how to minimize the usage of resources and cost; and 5) how to minimize makespan and cost of computation and data transfer.

the workflow management systems are a very important part of the scientific applications.
the current state of the art of workflow management systems is not mature and robust enough to handle the complex and dynamic nature of the data-intensive applications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have presented a comprehensive survey of scheduling and management techniques for data-intensive application workflows, which can be used as a reference for researchers in this field.
we have developed a framework that is able to handle the data-intensive application workflows in a distributed Grid system.
this chapter presents a survey of algorithms and techniques used by Grid systems for scheduling and managing data-intensive application workflows.

there is a wide variety of workflow management techniques available to the Grid community.
the data-intensive workflow scheduling problem can be solved using a variety of techniques.
the scheduling and execution techniques used by the workflow management systems can be broadly classified into two categories.
